name: FedEx Freight Holding Company, Inc.
moat_justification: Largest North American LTL network (365+ locations, 26,000+ doors, 98% of U.S. ZIP codes) and costly-to-replicate terminals give real density scale, but service is replicable, pricing is cyclical, and Old Dominion — not FDXF — is the service and margin leader; carve-out ROIC prints (62.5%/42.5%) are parent-capital artifacts and the first standalone print is 9.9% on negative equity.
fragility_flags: THIN_HISTORY: only 3 fiscal years of data
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share -1.50 vs 3-yr median 7.14 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 4.2x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.4%) vs bull-case tier C (10.1%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Largest North American LTL carrier with a real density moat (5/10), but a levered spin-off priced for a recovery it hasn't printed — at $113.58 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 8.2%, weighted IV@15% $51.88; hurdle price $51.88).
moat_for: Largest NA LTL carrier by revenue ($8,782M vs Old Dominion $5,446M) — densest network, 365+ locations / 26,000+ doors, 98% U.S. ZIP coverage
High barriers to entry: service-center terminals are costly and slow to build; top five carriers hold the majority of the market
Dual Priority/Economy model segments time-definite vs deferred freight off one network
Proprietary digital platforms (LTL Select) and route-optimization tooling
moat_against: Not the quality leader: Old Dominion ranked top national carrier in shipper surveys 16 straight years, with structurally higher margins
Operating margin fell 18.6% → 15.8% → 6.1% GAAP (FY2024–26); FY2026 adjusted 12.6%, below best-in-class LTL
Cyclical industrial demand: average daily shipments −4% FY2026, −5.9% in Q4; industry excess capacity pressures yield
Low shipper switching costs — freight is re-bid; Estes, XPO, Saia, R+L run comparable networks
Rising wage rates on a labor-dominant cost base
